\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Build --- Contract --- Lift: Results}

\begin{definition}[Lifting a contract to a larger alphabet]
\lean{Turing.Contract.liftSymbols}
\label{Turing.Contract.liftSymbols}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.decodeSymbols, Turing.Cfg.liftOver, Turing.Cfg.liftOver_decodeSymbols, Turing.Contract, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols_runFrom_over}
Let $e$ embed the two Boolean symbols into an alphabet, and let a machine with Boolean
symbols have transitions independent of the scanned input symbol and never write a blank
onto a work tape. For any contract for this machine on the input obtained by replacing
every symbol of a given input word by false, the lifted machine has a contract on that
word: its precondition, running time, endpoint, and head-position bounds are those of
the original contract applied to the configuration decoded through $e$.
\end{definition}
